evals.expected_output: The agent invokes the workspace-status backend (python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/workspace_status.py status --root <root>) and surfaces the initiative queue and repository backlog from the JSON output. For this fixture: one active initiative ('Example Initiative') with one queued item that is ready to start — spec/example-feature has no blocking dependencies, so the backend classifies it as ready even though no spec.md exists (missing spec files affect reconciliation, not readiness). It also renders 'Backlog — 2 open item(s)' followed, in source order, by the untyped example-build entry labeled [build] and the typed example-shape entry labeled [shape]. assertions: Invokes the backend script rather than independently parsing workspace.toml or recomputing the DAG
Reports the active initiative name from the JSON output ('Example Initiative')
Reports the queued spec as ready to start (no blocking dependencies in the fixture)
Renders a dynamically counted two-item Backlog section from repo_backlog.open
Reports example-build as [build] before example-shape as [shape]

evals.prompt: Show workspace status, including the tracker refresh authority and availability facts
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes the workspace-status backend and reports only its structured tracker authority projection: tracker-origin, profile example-service 1.0, compared revision remote-rev-2, accepted revision remote-rev-1, unresolved conflict, and refresh/write-back availability unknown. It does not expose field ownership, the approver identity, raw tracker content, or infer that a processor is installed.
assertions: Uses the backend authority projection rather than parsing prose or tracker content
Reports compared and accepted revisions plus the unresolved conflict
Reports refresh and write-back availability as unknown until a processor provides explicit facts
Does not expose owned fields or approver identity

evals.prompt: Show whether this all-shipped initiative can be closed and what I should do next.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses workspace-status only for a read-only projection of pause, closeout blockers, all-specs-shipped eligibility, cooling-context visibility, and the instruction to invoke close-work. assertions: Projects eligibility and blockers without choosing policy
Directs the user to close-work for closeout
Performs no write, compaction, or deletion

assertions: Uses the backend brief_queue projection
Preserves the scalar executing compatibility field
Names shipped, withdrawn, and cancelled terminal collections
Treats a Shipped child as execution evidence without automatic brief closure
